context: Tests whether an agent producing a plugin-publishing checklist correctly surfaces provenance sensitivity for third-party skills, warns about the irreversibility of making a plugin public, includes the required lint and dry-run steps, mentions auth requirements, bumps the version for a second release, and handles plugin retirement correctly.

checklist.name: Provenance concern raised
checklist.description: The checklist explicitly mentions that the plugin wraps skills authored by someone else (a colleague/third party) and states this must be addressed or confirmed before publishing

checklist.name: Public visibility confirmed
checklist.description: The checklist includes a step to confirm or explicitly set the plugin's visibility to public (i.e., changing or verifying the `private` field in plugin.json)

checklist.name: Public is irreversible warning
checklist.description: The checklist states that making a plugin public is irreversible — a public plugin cannot be made private again

checklist.name: Lint step included
checklist.description: The checklist includes running `tessl plugin lint` (with the plugin directory) as a required pre-publish step

checklist.name: Dry-run step included
checklist.description: The checklist includes running `tessl plugin publish --dry-run` (or equivalent) before the actual publish command

checklist.name: Auth requirement mentioned
checklist.description: The checklist mentions that publishing requires authentication via `tessl login` or the `TESSL_TOKEN` environment variable

checklist.name: Version bump step
checklist.description: The checklist includes bumping the plugin version (e.g., using `--bump patch`, `--bump minor`, `--bump major`, or editing the `version` field in plugin.json) since this is a second release

checklist.name: Retirement via archive, not unpublish
checklist.description: The note about taking the plugin down recommends `tessl plugin archive` as the standard approach, OR clearly states that `tessl plugin unpublish` only works within 2 days of publishing — does NOT present unpublish as a general rollback strategy
